profile.headline: Software Engineer | Robotics, Simulation & ML Systems | Ex-Meta FAIR
profile.summary: 20+ years of experience building robotics, simulation, and ML systems across Meta (FAIR Robotics), Cruise, Baidu, and the game industry.

positions.title: Staff Research Engineer
positions.description:
• Progressed through engineering and leadership roles within Meta’s Fundamental AI Research group (FAIR): Research Engineer → Tech Lead Manager → Software & Simulation Lead.

• Set simulation strategy for our 60-person organization; defined a unified simulation platform spanning physics, rendering, large-scale scene datasets, teleoperation, and RL tooling; achieved early adoption of the platform in two major dexterous-manipulation research efforts.

• Led software integration for FAIR Robotics’ prototype robot; assembled an end-to-end control stack from components built by multiple teams; coordinated cross-team dependencies to deliver a working system on schedule, within three months of hardware availability.

• Managed and grew the HABITAT engineering team; mentored engineers into higher-impact roles, including first-authorship opportunities.

• Helped initiate the PARTNR project; rallied contributors as it grew into one of FAIR Robotics’ largest collaborations; defined simulation platform features that enabled its novel human–robot collaboration results.

• Led the GALACTIC project, re-architecting our simulator and RL training pipeline for 100× higher throughput; cut mobile-pick skill training from >24 hours to 16 minutes; enabled billion-step-scale RL on low-cost hardware.

• Initiated the Habitat Synthetic Scenes Dataset, curating and licensing 200+ high-quality indoor scenes; it became FAIR Robotics’ most widely used scene dataset.

• Built and deployed VR and browser-based teleoperation and data-collection applications; collected over 100,000 expert demonstrations.

• Co-authored 10 papers accepted at ICLR, CVPR, NeurIPS, CoRL, and IEEE RA-L, focused on robotics research in simulation-driven policy learning for navigation and planning.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Technical lead for seven engineers building a core planning component for Cruise’s self-driving car.

• Translation of high-level behaviors into convex optimization problems.

• Graph algorithms, including multithreaded, deterministic graph search.

• Computational geometry, spatial data structures, and spatial queries for 3D environments.

• Low-level C++ performance optimizations: data structure layout, memory management, data locality.

• Iterative development via unit tests, simulation, and real-world test drives on the streets of San Francisco.

• Discussion/collaboration with Machine Learning teams (Tensorflow optimization, ML for Planning).

positions.title: Research Software Engineer
positions.description:
• ML systems researcher working at the intersection of large-scale neural network training, GPU performance, and applied research within an industry research lab.

• Worked with state-of-the-art deep neural networks for speech recognition, natural language processing, and text-to-speech; CNN and RNN architectures, optimizers.

• Researched weight sparsity for recurrent neural networks, including weight pruning, dropconnect, weight tying, and L1/L½/group-lasso regularization.

• Co-authored Block-sparse RNNs (NIPS 2017 poster, GTC 2018 talk, patent application 16/151,886).

• Built TensorFlow profiler to analyze GPU compute and memory utilization.

• Optimized the lab’s language model, yielding ~10x train speedup.

• Optimized network utilization for multi-GPU, multi-node training on the lab’s HPC cluster.

• Built DNN models in Python/TensorFlow and proprietary C++ machine learning framework.

• Studied low-precision training, memory-efficient backprop, model parallelism, and GEMM approximation.

• Researched operational intensity for various AI applications to predict speedup on future hardware.

positions.title: Lead Developer
positions.description:
• Built the STAR CONTROL PC title from the ground up, prototyping as the sole engineer, growing the team to five engineers, and leading the project’s technical direction, planning, and schedules.

• Integrated and extended Stardock’s early-in-development “Nitrous” multithreaded game engine.

• Researched networking model and coded initial multiplayer implementation, including serialization.

• Planet world editor, including terrain, static environments, placement/spawning of game entities.

• Spherical planet heightmap renderer with LOD and multitexturing.

• C# tools for editing dialog trees, scripts, and app-specific XML files. 

• Spaceship combat gameplay, including ship physics, gravity, projectiles, and AI ship behavior.

• Planet-surface gameplay, including AI enemy wander/aggro/attack behavior. 

• Integrated Bullet Physics library for vehicles and character movement in planet environments.

• Multithreaded performance optimization using Visual Studio Concurrency Visualizer and other tools.

• Wrote HLSL shaders for particle systems and planets; integrated post-processing effects.

• Added asynchronous tracing to engine to aid multithreaded debugging.

• Graphics debugging and optimization using Intel Graphics Performance Analyzers.

• FaceFX lipsync animation and script-driven mood animation for dialog scenes.

positions.title: Contract Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Senior contract engineer trusted by multiple studios to parachute into active productions and deliver critical gameplay, engine, and performance work across diverse stacks.

• Electronic Arts-Tiburon − Maitland, FL − Camera and depth-of-field shader for NBA LIVE 13.

• BioWare Austin − Austin, TX − Frostbite engine, Havok physics, decal rendering, and character movement for an unannounced PC game.  

• SecretNewCo/Big Huge Games – Baltimore, MD − Unity, pathfinding, shaders, memory profiling, and optimization for DomiNations mobile game.

• Bully! Entertainment − Baltimore, MD − Unity, physics, camera, optimization, and Objective-C plugin for PELE: KING OF FOOTBALL mobile game and other apps.

• North Side Inc. − Montreal, Canada − BOTCOLONY PC game. I led four engineers in the transition of their in-house engine to the Havok Vision engine. Pathfinding, Havok physics, Morpheme animation, SpeedTree.

• Backflip Studios − Boulder, CO − Objective-C, pathfinding, and Havok physics for iOS games.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Senior engineer on KINGDOMS OF AMALUR: RECKONING , contributing core gameplay and engine-level systems.

• Intelligent third-person camera, including enemy framing and obstacle avoidance.  See my in-depth article in Game Developer Magazine, September 2011.

• Havok Physics integration: collision geometry pipeline, character movement, streaming Havok data, ragdolls, chains, inverse kinematics, and collision queries.

• Vegetation system for grass and other ground clutter.  Tool-side: real-time brushing onto terrain, a layer system, and custom control over instancing.  Runtime: streaming, batched rendering, wind, and distance LOD.  

• Terrain texture streaming.  Terrain shader to blend detail ground textures.

• Minimap rendering, including triangulation of road splines and a shader to handle multi-floor interiors.

• General memory profiling, performance profiling, and optimizing.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
As sole producer and engineer, developed a PC racing game intended for digital distribution.  Responsible for game design, art contracting, music licensing, and software engineering.  Programmed systems to meet the unique requirements of the game design, including:

• Physics simulator, including rigid bodies, continuous collision detection, ragdolls, friction, and aerodynamics for aircraft.  Detailed, accurate “bullet-time” replays.

• Deterministic, replayable game simulation framework, with automated determinism-checking during replays.

• Large-scale terrain renderer; supports dynamic LOD and USGS elevation data.

• Unique, science-fiction, roller-coaster-style race track with custom track editor.

• 3D models: support for skeletal animation, skinning, and geometry instancing.

• Graphical effects, including real-time shadows (via shadow mapping), variable-width 3D lines, real-time posterization, and “wireframe traversal” visualization.  

• GUI system for game menus and tutorial messages. It’s XML-driven and supports clickable text links, custom fonts and symbols, and various animation effects.

• DirectX utilities for robust device-loss-handling (“alt-tabbing”) and input device management (mouse, keyboard, joysticks, gamepads).

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Worked on NFL STREET, an original, first-year title for PS2, Xbox, and NGC.

• Added specular lighting (with gloss maps) to the Xbox character lighting model.  

• Handled PAL versions of game for Xbox, PS2, and NGC.

• Worked to satisfy Microsoft TCR and Sony TRC for memory card features.



Helped bring Xbox Live functionality to MADDEN NFL 2005, NCAA FOOTBALL 2005, and NASCAR 2005.  These were among the first EA titles to support Xbox Live.

• Wrote a helper class for simulating high latency; tested online play.

• Ported online leaderboard and other Flash screens to Xbox.



Performed research and prototyping for an unreleased console title.  Worked closely with the project’s Lead Programmer on all core graphics and physics systems.

• Implemented a space partitioning system to accelerate collision-detection and visibility culling (a hybrid kd-tree/BSP-tree).

• Implemented a custom “height-line” occlusion-culling system.

• Integrated existing terrain with Havok's collision-detection system.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
Worked on MADDEN NFL 2002 for PC. Just previously, the franchise had made the leap to PS2 as one of the console’s most impressive launch titles. Within a short development cycle, our small engineering team successfully ported the ground-breaking new simulation and graphics technologies from the PS2 to the PC.

• Ported various PS2 render code to D3D (character shadows, snow, rain, sun and stadium-light flares, character breath fog, footprints, real-time field degradation).

• Implemented a GPU-based occlusion query.

• Implemented stadium shadows (GPU-generated lightmaps).
